screening_decisions.reason: Randomized double‑blind placebo‑controlled crossover trial of oral inosiplex in alopecia totalis – meets RCT criteria for a systemic intervention.
Placebo‑controlled, parallel‑group randomized trial of oral pulse prednisolone (systemic corticosteroid) in extensive alopecia areata.
Randomised, investigator‑blinded parallel‑group trial comparing two topical corticosteroid formulations in mild‑to‑moderate alopecia areata.
Double‑blind, placebo‑controlled trial of 3 % topical minoxidil versus vehicle in extensive alopecia areata/totalis/universalis.
Randomised, double‑blind, parallel‑group trial of 3 % topical minoxidil (long‑term) versus placebo in extensive alopecia areata.
Randomised, split‑scalp, double‑blind trial evaluating topical diphenylcyclopropenone alone and in combination with 5 % minoxidil (both topical) in chronic severe alopecia areata.

Randomised allocation of three active treatments (topical cyclosporine, PUVA, intravenous thymopentin) to patients with alopecia totalis/universalis; although no placebo arm, it is a randomised interventional study.
Small uncontrolled case series of topical photodynamic therapy; no randomisation or control group.
Randomised, double‑blind, vehicle‑controlled trial of topical cyclosporin A in alopecia areata.
Double‑blind, placebo‑controlled randomised trial of oral imipramine (systemic) in alopecia areata.
Randomised three‑arm trial comparing topical immunotherapy, systemic interferon‑α, and their combination in chronic severe alopecia areata; qualifies as an RCT of topical and systemic interventions.
Double‑blind, placebo‑controlled randomised trial of topical cyclosporin A in 85 patients with alopecia areata.
Randomised, double‑blind, placebo‑controlled trial of clobetasol propionate 0.05 % foam (topical corticosteroid) in moderate‑to‑severe alopecia areata.
Randomised controlled trial of systemic prednisone taper followed by either topical minoxidil or vehicle – evaluates both systemic and topical therapy.
Randomised, double‑blind, placebo‑controlled trial of topical minoxidil (3 %) with long‑term follow‑up in extensive alopecia areata.
Controlled trial (randomised) comparing several active agents (squaric acid dibutylester, diphencyprone, minoxidil) with placebo in patchy alopecia areata (<40 % scalp involvement).
Survey of patient perceptions; no intervention, not a trial.
Conceptual commentary on when randomised trials are unnecessary; not a primary trial.
Randomised, double‑blind, placebo‑controlled trial of aromatherapy (essential oil massage) versus carrier oil in alopecia areata – meets RCT criteria.
Narrative update/review article; no primary trial data.
Epidemiological incidence study; not an interventional trial.
Observational prognostic factor analysis; no randomised intervention.
Randomised three‑arm trial comparing inosine pranobex, diphencyprone, and their combination in alopecia totalis – qualifies as an RCT of systemic and topical agents.
Genetic review article; not a primary trial.
Methodological review of trial quality; no primary data.
